pattern: Abstract meme/trend searches in crypto communities as primary strategy
why_wrong: By September 2026, tokenization velocity is so high that search-result memes are already late — they either have tokens or will imminently. Better strategy: hunt in non-crypto-native communities (mainstream trending, animal/news moments, specific communities) and look for moments with name/hook potential BEFORE they reach crypto Twitter.

pattern: Relying on broad X searches for "viral" or "trending" in real-time to catch pre-tokenized moments
why_wrong: By the time something is indexed and surfaced by X search (even live search), it's either already tokenized, already 12+ hours old, or it's noise from old posts. Better approach: identify specific name/hook the moment you spot it organically, then search THAT specific term to see if it's crossed into crypto Twitter yet. Or search very specific, just-launched things (like repo names, product names) before they get picked up widely.

pattern: Using abstract "viral," "trending," or activity-based searches (e.g., "what is everyone talking about") as primary strategy for finding pre-tokenized moments
why_wrong: By the time something is indexed and surfaced by X live search, it's either already too late (either tokenized, resolved by a news event, or past its emergence window), or it's noise from stale posts. Pre-tokenized moments have their name/hook established in replies and niche communities BEFORE they reach the trending tab. Better to search specific named things once you spot the hook organically, or monitor specific low-latency spaces (niche communities, early reply chains) rather than cast generic trend nets.
